description: Canonical fixtures for the runner↔supervisor stdout contract v1: NDJSON lines on the runner's stdout. Emitted by @decent-render/runner-core (src/index.ts, writeEvent); parsed by crates/supervisor-core/src/runner.rs (RunnerEvent, internally tagged on `type`). @decent-render/runner-core validates emitted events against runnerEventSchema and asserts every case here (src/__tests__/runner-stdout-conformance.test.ts); supervisor-core parses the SAME file in runner_stdout_fixtures_round_trip (runner.rs tests). The `accept` list is what both sides agree on today; the `reject` list is the negative contract — every entry MUST fail to parse on BOTH sides, so a schema that silently loosens (progress 1.5, a done without its output size, unknown types) is caught here.

wire.message: Render timed out: no progress for 120s

reject.name: unknown event type
reject.reason: progress, heartbeat, done, error are the whole contract; an unknown type is some foreign process writing to stdout

reject.name: progress out of range (1.5)
reject.reason: progress is a fraction in [0, 1] on both sides — protocol v2's jobProgress carries the identical bound, and dispatch would refuse to persist 1.5 anyway

reject.name: done missing outputSizeInBytes
reject.reason: the done envelope always carries the output size; the supervisor stamps it onto the metrics dispatch persists

reject.name: error missing message
reject.reason: an error without a message cannot be surfaced to the operator

reject.name: non-object line (renderer chatter)
reject.reason: stdout is NDJSON; a bare string is renderer chatter. The supervisor tolerates it AT RUNTIME (warn + continue) so chatter cannot kill a job, but it is not a contract event and the schema must reject it
